title: How often the permit and fee rules change
question: How many ordinances touching permits and fees are enacted each year, and do they add steps or remove them?
finding: 953 ordinances touching permits, fees or the codes that govern them were enacted from 2018 to 2026, about 106 a year. By the wording of their titles, 219 add a requirement, restriction or fee and 205 streamline, waive or exempt (59 do both). The balance has shifted: through 2021, 24% of ordinances added and 17% removed; since 2023, 21% added and 28% removed. 64 raise or create a fee and 78 waive, cut or defer one. 87 are landmark designations, which add a review for one building, and 128 are budget, bond, lawsuit or agreement items left unsorted.
how: The index lists every enacted ordinance, introduced since 2017 and passed 2018 to 2026, whose title mentions permits, fees, a regulatory code, streamlining, conditional use or notice. Appropriations, bond measures, lawsuit settlements and agreements were set aside by their short titles. Each of the rest was put into groups by keyword rules applied to its short title and long title as filed (the rules are in the script). An ordinance can fall in several groups.
limits: The sorting is rough: in a spot check of 22 sorted titles about one in five sat in a wrong or doubtful group. A title is not the law: an ordinance that "amends the Planning Code to require" something may also relax something else in its text, and many titles use none of the keywords. The index was built by keyword, so it includes landmark designations, zoning maps and appropriations that touch permits only loosely; they are counted separately. Counting ordinances does not measure how many people each one affects. Frequent change is a cost to applicants whichever way it points, and both adding and removing rules are ordinary acts of a legislature.
